slides.texte_overlay:
Small daily habits
of grateful men
They write three good things every night. Small or big, it doesn't matter. Their brain slowly learns to notice what's going right.
They thank people by name. "Thanks, Marco." Using someone's name makes gratitude personal and memorable. People remember it.
They enjoy simple things. A hot shower, a good meal, a sunny morning. Noticing small pleasures makes every day feel richer.
They tell people why they appreciate them. Not just "thanks," but "you really helped me with that." Specific gratitude means more.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Learning how the world works makes you grateful for things you took for granted.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Learning how the world works makes you grateful for things you took for granted.

slides.texte_overlay: They complain less. When something goes wrong, they look for a fix instead of someone to blame. It keeps their energy positive.
They give back. Helping a friend, volunteering, teaching someone. Grateful men share what they've received. Pass it on.
